breadcrumb: Std 6 Social Science Term-III (English) — History Unit 2: The Post-Mauryan India — Boxed notes (தெரிந்து தெளிவோம் / Do you know)

questions.quote: Pushyamitra thwarted an attack from the Kalinga king Kharavela. He also conquered Vidarba. He was a staunch follower of Vedic religion. He performed two Asvamedha yagnas.

en.q: Pushyamitra thwarted an attack from the Kalinga king ______.
en.explanation: He successfully repulsed the invasion of the Bactrian king Menander, too.

ta.q: புஷ்யமித்ரர் கலிங்க மன்னன் ______ இன் தாக்குதலை முறியடித்தார்.

questions.quote: Pushyamitra was succeeded by his son Agnimitra. This Agnimitra is said to be the hero of Kalidasa's Malavikagnimitra. The drama also refers to the victory of Vasumitra, Agnimitra's son, over the Greeks on the banks of the Sindhu river.

en.q: Agnimitra is said to be the hero of Kalidasa's drama ______.
en.explanation: Vasumitra, Agnimitra's son, defeated the Greeks on the banks of the Sindhu.

ta.explanation: அக்னிமித்ரரின் மகன் வசுமித்ரர் சிந்து கரையில் கிரேக்கரை வென்றார்.

questions.quote: The Sunga dynasty lasted for about one hundred years. The last Sunga king was Devabhuti. He was killed by his own minister Vasudeva Kanva.

en.q: The Sunga dynasty lasted for about ______ years.
en.explanation: Their weak successors faced threats from the Indo-Bactrians and Indo-Parthians.

ta.explanation: பலவீனமான வாரிசுகள் இந்தோ-பாக்ட்ரியர், இந்தோ-பார்த்தியரின் அச்சுறுத்தலை எதிர்கொண்டனர்.

questions.quote: Patanjali, the second grammarian in Sanskrit, was patronized by Pushyamitra. The Sungas revived Vedic religious practices and promoted Vaishnavism. Sanskrit gradually gained ascendancy and became the court language.

en.q: Patanjali, patronised by Pushyamitra, was the ______ in Sanskrit.
en.explanation: Sanskrit gradually became the court language.

questions.quote: Gautamiputra Satakarni was the greatest ruler of the family. In the Nasik eulogy, published by his mother Gautami Balasri, he is described as the destroyer of Sakas, Yavanas (Greeks) and Pahlavas (Parthians).

en.q: The greatest ruler of the Satavahana family was ______.
options: Hala, the poet-king and author of Sattasai
en.explanation: The Nasik eulogy by his mother Gautami Balasri describes him as the destroyer of Sakas, Yavanas and Pahlavas.

ta.explanation: தாய் கௌதமி பாலஸ்ரீயின் நாசிக் புகழுரை இவரைச் சகர், யவனர், பஹ்லவர் அழித்தவர் எனக் கூறுகிறது.

questions.quote: The Satavahana ship coins are suggestive of Andhras' skill in seafaring and naval power.

en.q: The ship coins of the Satavahanas show their skill in ______.
en.explanation: The later Satavahana kings issued lead or bronze coins depicting ships with two masts.

ta.q: சாதவாகனரின் கப்பல் நாணயங்கள் அவர்களின் ______ திறனைக் காட்டுகின்றன.
ta.explanation: இரு பாய்மரக் கப்பல் பொறித்த ஈயம், வெண்கல நாணயங்கள் வெளியிடப்பட்டன.

questions.quote: The Satavahana rulers were great builders. They began constructing Buddhist stupas in Amaravati. The Mathura School of Sculpture produced images and life-size statues of the Buddhist, Brahmanical and Jain deities.

en.q: The Satavahanas began constructing Buddhist stupas at ______.
en.explanation: Gandhara, Mathura, Amaravati, Bodh Gaya, Sanchi and Bharhut were known for monuments and art.

ta.q: சாதவாகனர் பௌத்த ஸ்தூபிகள் கட்டத் தொடங்கிய இடம் ______.
ta.explanation: காந்தாரம், மதுரா, அமராவதி, புத்தகயா, சாஞ்சி, பர்ஹுத் ஆகியவை கலைக்குப் புகழ்பெற்றவை.

questions.quote: Demetrius issued bi-lingual square coins with Greek on the obverse and Kharosthi on the reverse. Menander: MilindaPanha, a Buddhist text, is a discourse between Bactrian king Milinda and the learned Buddhist scholar Nagasena. This Milinda is identified with Menander.

en.q: The Buddhist text 'Milinda Panha' is a discourse between King Milinda (Menander) and the Buddhist scholar ______.
en.explanation: Menander is believed to have become a Buddhist.

ta.q: 'மிலிந்த பன்ஹா' என்ற பௌத்த நூல் மன்னன் மிலிந்தாவுக்கும் (மினாண்டர்) பௌத்த அறிஞர் ______ க்கும் இடையிலான உரையாடல்.

questions.quote: Coinage: Indo-Greek rulers introduced a die system and produced properly shaped coins with inscription, symbols and engraved figures on them. Sculpture: The Gandhara School of Indian Art is heavily indebted to Greek influence.

en.q: The Gandhara School of Indian Art was heavily indebted to ______ influence.
en.explanation: Indians also learnt the die system of coinage from the Indo-Greeks.

ta.q: இந்தியக் காந்தாரக் கலைப் பாணி பெரிதும் ______ தாக்கம் பெற்றது.
ta.explanation: அச்சு முறை நாணயத்தையும் இந்தியர் இந்தோ-கிரேக்கரிடம் கற்றனர்.

questions.quote: Sakas were Scythians, nomadic ancient Iranians, and known as Sakas in Sanskrit. Saka rule was founded by Maues or Moga in the Gandhara region. The Sakas appointed kshatrapas or satraps as provincial governors.

en.q: The provincial governors appointed by the Sakas were called ______.
en.explanation: Rudradaman was the most important Saka king.

questions.quote: Indo-Parthian kingdom or Gondopharid dynasty was founded by Gondophernes. The domain of Indo-Parthians comprised Kabul and Gandhara. The name of Gondophernes is associated with the Christian apostle St. Thomas.

en.q: The domain of the Indo-Parthians comprised ______.
en.explanation: The Indo-Parthian kingdom is also called the Gondopharid dynasty.

ta.explanation: இந்தோ-பார்த்திய அரசு கோண்டோபெரிட் வம்சம் எனவும் அழைக்கப்படும்.

questions.quote: The Kushanas formed a section of the yueh-chi tribes, who inhabited north-western China in the remote past. Kushana rulers were Buddhists. Takshashila and Mathura continued to be great centres of Buddhist learning.

en.q: The Kushanas formed a section of the ______ tribes who originally inhabited north-western China.
en.explanation: Takshashila and Mathura attracted students from China and western Asia.

ta.q: குஷாணர் பண்டைக் காலத்தில் வடமேற்குச் சீனாவில் வாழ்ந்த ______ இனத்தின் ஒரு பிரிவினர்.
ta.explanation: தட்சசீலமும் மதுராவும் பௌத்தக் கல்வி மையங்களாகத் திகழ்ந்தன.

questions.quote: Kanishka was the greatest of all the Kushana emperors. He assumed the sovereignty in 78 AD and proclaimed his rule by the foundation of a new era, which later became Saka era. The Kushana capital initially was Kabul. Later, it was shifted to Peshavar or Purushpura.

en.q: Kanishka assumed sovereignty in ______ and began a new era that later became the Saka era.
en.explanation: The Kushana capital was shifted from Kabul to Peshawar (Purushapura).

ta.q: கனிஷ்கர் ______ இல் ஆட்சிக்கு வந்து புதிய ஆண்டைத் தொடங்கினார்; அது பின்னர் சக ஆண்டாயிற்று.

questions.quote: Kanishka organised the fourth Buddhist Council at Kundalavana near Srinagar to sort out the differences between the various schools of Buddhism. It was only in this council that Buddhism was split into Hinayanism and Mahayanism. His court was adorned with Buddhist saints and scholars, like Asvaghosha, Vasumitra and Nagarjuna.

en.q: The Post-Mauryan India: Which of the following scholars adorned the court of Kanishka?
en.explanation: The others were Vasumitra and Nagarjuna.

questions.quote: Kushana Empire corresponded with the last days of the Roman Republic, when Julius Caesar was alive. It is said that Kushana Emperor sent a great embassy to Augustus Caesar.

en.q: According to the textbook, the Kushana emperor sent a great embassy to the Roman emperor ______.
en.explanation: This is the textbook's statement; historically the Kushana Empire began only in the 1st century CE, after Augustus.

ta.q: பாடநூலின்படி, குஷாணப் பேரரசர் ரோமப் பேரரசர் ______ இடம் பெரும் தூதுக்குழுவை அனுப்பினார்.
ta.explanation: இது பாடநூலின் கூற்று; வரலாற்றில் குஷாணப் பேரரசு அகஸ்டஸுக்குப் பின், பொ.ஆ. முதல் நூற்றாண்டிலேயே தோன்றியது.
